comparator.name: Bachelor Electrical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's official programme pages, checked 2026-09-29, describe a three-year Dutch-language Electrical Engineering bachelor centred on physics, mathematics, circuits, digital systems, energy, telecommunications, electronics, signals and control. The current EEMCS curriculum-chart portal still publicly links the official 2025-2026 Electrical Engineering chart. That chart accounts for the complete 180 EC as twelve 15-EC quarters: eight compulsory quarters in years one and two, a 30-EC first-semester minor in year three, a 15-EC advanced-course quarter and a 15-EC bachelor graduation project. Quarter blocks preserve all named courses and the chart's exact credit structure without inventing within-quarter EC allocations that the public chart does not print.

programmes.label: Bachelor Electrical Engineering at Delft University of Technology

exception.reason: TU Delft's bachelor is a cumulative electrical-engineering education in circuit theory, analogue and digital electronics, electricity and magnetism, electrical energy, signals and systems, telecommunications and sensing, electromagnetics, semiconductor devices, mixed-signal systems, control, signal processing, computer architecture and repeated hardware-focused integrated projects before a 15-EC Electrical Engineering graduation project. UCR offers a useful mathematics, computing, data-science, robotics and renewable-energy-adjacent set, but it has no electricity-and-magnetism physics course, circuit or electronics sequence, semiconductor-device course, electrical measurements laboratory, telecommunications/sensing sequence or electrical-engineering hardware project sequence. A 24-course UCR response would be a mathematics-and-computing programme with some energy and robotics applications, not Electrical Engineering.
exception.curriculumContext: The latest Electrical Engineering curriculum chart publicly linked by TU Delft's current EEMCS portal accounts for the complete 180 EC: four 15-EC quarters in year one, four 15-EC quarters in year two, a genuine 30-EC minor in the first half of year three, a 15-EC quarter of signal processing, computer architecture and an elective, and a 15-EC Electrical Engineering bachelor graduation project. The sequence progresses from linear circuits, digital systems, calculus, electricity and magnetism, and energy fundamentals through transistor and mixed-signal circuits, signals and control, telecommunications, electromagnetics and semiconductor physics. Integrated Projects 1-3 have explicit prerequisite chains, and the graduation project requires all first- and second-year courses.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics cover important mathematical foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISCOMP211 Networks & Operating Systems, DISDATA211 Machine Learning, DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision, DISDATA312 Robotics and the AI sequence provide relevant computation and applications. ENSGATE101 Sustainability Essentials I, ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design and BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design add broad physical-science, energy-system and prototyping contexts. The workbook nevertheless contains no dedicated electricity and magnetism, linear or transistor circuits, analogue or digital electronics, semiconductor physics, electrical machines or power electronics, electromagnetic fields, telecommunications and sensing, instrumentation laboratory, computer hardware architecture, or integrated electrical-engineering design project. ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability is adjacent but has no offering in the six-term planning window. The available mathematics and software cannot substitute for the target's compulsory experimental hardware and electronics spine.
